name: Cancel a charge billed in error against which no money has been received
priorityReason: Invoices are raised in bulk, so wrong ones are raised in bulk. Without this the only remedy is editing a bill, which the format forbids.

goal.capability: to undo a charge that should never have been raised and has not been paid
goal.outcome: the family owes the right amount, and the books show both what was billed and what was undone

secondaryActors.involvement: Approves the cancellation. Accounts cannot cancel a charge alone.
Is billed the corrected amount and is told the original was cancelled.

additional.description: A whole batch is found to have been raised wrongly, and each invoice in it is cancelled as a unit.

preconditions.condition: An issued invoice exists against which no payment has been received (BR-2).

establishedBy.name: Issuing fee invoices at different scopes

preconditions.condition: An authenticated session exists. Raising requires Accounts; approving requires School Admin.
A chart of accounts exists, so the balancing entry can post.

establishedBy.name: Reading the books: ledger, trial balance and journals

preconditions.condition: The accounting period the original invoice was raised in is still open, or the cancellation posts to the current one (BR-9).

postConditions: The invoice reads Cancelled and is no longer owed by the family or counted in the school's receivables.
A balancing entry has posted to the ledger, and the original entry is still there. Nothing has been deleted or edited.
The invoice has left overdue tracking and stops accruing any late fee.
Any concession or family credit the invoice consumed has been returned, so a discount is not lost because a wrong bill was cancelled.
The correct charge can now be raised in its place through the ordinary invoice run.
The family has been told the original charge was cancelled, so a challan already in their hands is not paid by mistake.
Any challan printed for the invoice is void, and paying it would settle nothing.
The cancellation carries its reason, who raised it and who approved it, so a bill that vanished can be explained.

businessRules.rule: A cancellation is raised by one person and approved by another. The role that bills cannot also undo a bill unaided, because a charge that can be raised and removed by one hand is a charge nobody can rely on.
This use case applies only where no money has been received. A charge that was wrong but has been paid is a credit, not a cancellation, because the school is holding money that is not its own.
A cancellation is for the whole invoice. Cancelling part of a bill is a different act, done by cancelling the invoice and raising the correct one in its place.
A reason and a written description are mandatory. An invoice that disappeared with no explanation is the thing an auditor asks about first.
A balancing entry posts to the ledger and the original entry stays in place. Nothing is deleted and nothing is edited, so the books show both what was billed and what was undone.
The invoice itself is never edited. Its status moves to Cancelled and its lines are left exactly as they were.
Any concession or family credit the invoice consumed is returned. A family must not lose a discount because the school billed them wrongly.

A whole batch raised in error may be cancelled as a unit. Every unpaid invoice in it is cancelled; any that has been paid is refused and listed, because money received is not undone by cancelling a bill.
Where the original invoice's accounting period has closed, the cancellation posts to the current open period. A closed period is not reopened to tidy a mistake.
Cancelling raises nothing in its place. The correct charge is raised through the ordinary invoice run, as a separate and deliberate act.
The family is told the charge was cancelled, so a challan already in their hands is not paid by mistake.
A cancelled invoice leaves overdue tracking and stops accruing late fee at once, so a family is not chased or fined for a bill the school has withdrawn.

transitions.condition: Approved. The balancing entry posts and the invoice moves to Cancelled (BR-5).
Returned with a reason. The invoice is untouched and still owed.

basicFlow.userAction: Identifies a charge billed in error, for the wrong amount, or against the wrong student, with no money received against it.
basicFlow.systemResponse: Checks no payment has been recorded against the invoice, and refuses where one has.

basicFlow.navigation: Student invoice → Cancel charge → Raise cancellation
basicFlow.userAction: Raises the cancellation, selecting the reason and describing what went wrong.
basicFlow.systemResponse: Requires a reason and a description, and sets the cancellation to Awaiting approval.

basicFlow.userAction: Reviews the cancellation and approves it.
basicFlow.systemResponse: Records the approval with who gave it and when.
Posts the balancing entry to the ledger and the reversing entry to the student ledger. The original entries stay in place.
Sets the invoice to Cancelled without editing it, voids any challan printed for it, and returns any concession or family credit it consumed.
Tells the family the charge was cancelled, so a challan already in their hands is not paid by mistake.

basicFlow.userAction: Raises the correct charge through the ordinary invoice run.
basicFlow.systemResponse: The correct invoice is raised as a separate, deliberate act.

alternateFlows.condition: A whole batch was raised in error
alternateFlows.navigation: Login → Fee → Issue batches → Cancel batch
alternateFlows.behaviour: Every unpaid invoice in the batch is cancelled as a unit. Any that has been paid is refused and listed, because money received is not undone by cancelling a bill (BR-8).

alternateFlows.condition: Money has been received against the charge
alternateFlows.behaviour: This is not a cancellation. A credit is raised instead, because the school is holding money that is not its own (BR-2).

alternateFlows.condition: The School Admin does not accept the cancellation
alternateFlows.behaviour: It returns to Accounts with a written reason. The invoice is untouched and still owed in the meantime.

alternateFlows.condition: The invoice consumed a concession or a family credit
alternateFlows.behaviour: Both are returned, so a family does not lose a discount because the school billed them wrongly (BR-7).

alternateFlows.condition: The original invoice's accounting period has closed
alternateFlows.behaviour: The cancellation posts to the current open period rather than reopening a closed one to tidy a mistake (BR-9).

alternateFlows.condition: The invoice has already accrued a late fee
alternateFlows.behaviour: The fine is cancelled with the charge, since a family is not fined for a bill the school has withdrawn (BR-12).

exceptions.condition: A payment has been recorded against the invoice
exceptions.systemResponse: The cancellation is refused and the credit route is named (BR-2).
exceptions.messageShown: PKR 4,000 was received against this invoice on 08-09-2026. Raise a credit instead.

exceptions.condition: No reason or description is given
exceptions.messageShown: Describe what went wrong. A cancelled charge has to be explainable.

exceptions.condition: Accounts attempt to approve their own cancellation
exceptions.messageShown: Only a School Admin can approve a cancellation.

exceptions.condition: The invoice has already been cancelled
The invoice has been written off
exceptions.messageShown: This debt was written off on 20-11-2026. A cancellation does not apply to it.

exceptions.systemResponse: The whole cancellation is rolled back. The invoice is still owed and the cancellation stays awaiting approval.
exceptions.messageShown: The cancellation could not be posted. Nothing has changed.

exceptions.condition: A batch cancellation is raised where some invoices have been paid
exceptions.systemResponse: The unpaid ones are cancelled and the paid ones are refused and listed (BR-8).
exceptions.messageShown: 18 of 20 invoices cancelled. 2 have been paid — raise a credit for those.

exceptions.condition: The message to the family fails
exceptions.systemResponse: The cancellation stands and the send is marked Failed. It can be resent. A cancellation is never undone because a message failed.
exceptions.messageShown: The charge is cancelled. The message could not be sent — resend it from the cancellation.

departures.requirement: The original invoice and its ledger entry are never altered. A cancellation is always an additional entry, so the books read as a history rather than a current state.
The status change, both ledger postings and the restoration of concession and credit commit together or not at all.
A batch cancellation of 500 invoices completes within 60 seconds with a per-invoice result.
Cancellations and their postings are retained 7 years as financial records.

openQuestions.question: Should a cancellation be possible after the academic session has closed?
openQuestions.assumption: Yes, posting to the current period (BR-9). Not confirmed.

openQuestions.question: Is there a value above which the Principal rather than the School Admin should approve?
openQuestions.assumption: Not specified, and a large cancellation is a governance matter.

openQuestions.question: Should cancelling automatically offer to raise the corrected charge, or are the two entirely separate?
openQuestions.assumption: Separate (BR-10). Confirm the office does not want them linked.

openQuestions.question: Who reviews cancellations, and how often?
openQuestions.assumption: Not specified. Write-offs are reviewed separately; cancellations are not.

conventionsApplied.name: session-and-authentication
conventionsApplied.rule: Every use case except the login use case assumes an authenticated session. Sign out is available on every screen. An expired or invalid session returns the user to the login screen with the message "Your session has ended. Please sign in again."

conventionsApplied.name: role-based-access
conventionsApplied.rule: Access is enforced server-side on every request, not only by hiding menu items. A request for a record outside the actor's permitted scope returns a 403 and the message "You do not have permission to view this record." A use case states additions and restrictions only.

conventionsApplied.name: branch-scope
conventionsApplied.rule: Every record carries a branch ID. Users see only their own branch unless the use case states otherwise. Super Admin, School Admin and Principal may switch branch from the header.

conventionsApplied.name: academic-session-scope
conventionsApplied.rule: Every academic record carries an academic session ID. Lists default to the current open session.

conventionsApplied.name: list-screens
conventionsApplied.rule: Every list supports search, column sort and page-size selection. Default page size 25; default sort is most recent first. Filters are applied before printing or exporting.

conventionsApplied.name: print-and-pdf
conventionsApplied.rule: Every report and list offers Print and Download as PDF, honouring the filters currently applied. Each output carries the school name, branch, academic session, report title, filter summary, generation timestamp and the name of the user who generated it.

conventionsApplied.name: audit-trail
conventionsApplied.rule: Every create, update, deactivation, approval and reversal writes to the audit log: actor, role, timestamp, record type, record ID, before and after values, and IP address. Audit entries are never editable.

conventionsApplied.name: deletion
conventionsApplied.rule: Records are deactivated, not physically removed. Deactivated records are excluded from lists and lookups but remain in the audit trail and in historical reports. A record referenced by a financial transaction can never be deactivated.

conventionsApplied.name: validation-and-messages
conventionsApplied.rule: Field-level errors appear inline beneath the field on blur and on submit. Errors that block the whole action appear as a banner at the top of the form. Successful actions show a toast. No action succeeds silently.

conventionsApplied.name: money
conventionsApplied.rule: All monetary values are stored as fixed-point decimals in the smallest currency unit, never as floating point. Displayed as PKR with a thousands separator and two decimal places. Rounding is half-up at the line.

conventionsApplied.name: dates-times-numbers
conventionsApplied.rule: Dates display as DD-MM-YYYY; date and time as DD-MM-YYYY HH:mm in 24-hour form. Times are school-local. Phone numbers are stored in the registered mobile format.

conventionsApplied.name: language
conventionsApplied.rule: All user-visible strings come from a resource file. No hard-coded text in any screen.

conventionsApplied.name: concurrency-and-locking
conventionsApplied.rule: Last write wins, except where a use case defines an approval lock. Once a record is approved, posted or issued it becomes read-only and can only be changed through its defined reversal use case.

conventionsApplied.name: screen-states
conventionsApplied.rule: Every list, dashboard tile and report defines four states: loading, empty, error and populated. The empty state names what is missing and links to the action that creates it.

conventionsApplied.name: bulk-actions
conventionsApplied.rule: Any bulk operation reports a per-row result, commits valid rows and lists rejected rows with the reason. A bulk action never fails as a whole because of one bad row.

conventionsApplied.name: notifications
conventionsApplied.rule: All outbound SMS, WhatsApp, email and push messages are sent through the Messaging module, recorded in the sent-message log with per-channel delivery status, and use a named template. Use cases reference the template; they do not embed message text.

conventionsApplied.name: default-performance-and-retention
conventionsApplied.rule: Unless a use case states otherwise: a screen loads within 2 seconds and a save completes within 2 seconds at 200 concurrent users; lists paginate above 100 rows; financial and student records are retained 7 years; audit and message logs 12 months; every screen is usable at a 360 px viewport. Fill the non-functional field only to depart from this.

conventionsApplied.name: default-trigger
conventionsApplied.rule: Unless a use case states otherwise, the trigger is: the user navigates to the screen and initiates the action. Fill the Triggers field only where a scheduled job, an event in another module, or an inbound external call also starts it.
